runs.title: Texas just broke the “no AI hiring signal” story. It did not prove layoffs.
runs.summary: A Texas posting analysis adds a regional AI-exposure warning, while broad U.S. posting results still limit any national conclusion.

runs.title: The early-career AI warning just hit a hard Nordic counter-signal.
runs.summary: Population-wide Norwegian records find no robust young-worker employment displacement, sharpening the country and attribution limits on U.S. exposure-based warnings.

runs.title: The first AI-spending jobs test points up. The entry-level verdict is still open.
runs.summary: A firm-level spending proxy adds an actual-adoption counterpoint to the exposure-based early-career warning without resolving causal attribution.

runs.title: The 19% early-career gap got bigger. The causal fight did too.
runs.summary: A revised payroll study reinforces the concentrated U.S. early-career warning, while a cross-country remote-work result makes the attribution question sharper.

runs.title: A second Census study raises the stakes for AI-exposed graduates. It still is not a final verdict.
runs.summary: A new Census graduate study strengthens the concentrated U.S. early-career warning, while broad job-posting research finds no distinct AI-driven decline.

runs.title: The first hard warning is early-career hiring. It is not yet a clean AI verdict.
runs.summary: A U.S. working paper finds a sharp relative decline in early-career hiring in high-AI-exposure industries, while its AI attribution remains unresolved.
